tip.title: Do five minutes of cyclic sighing
tip.why: A Stanford trial published in Cell Reports Medicine in 2023 compared three five-minute breathing exercises with mindfulness meditation, done daily for a month. Cyclic sighing, which stretches the exhale, improved mood the most and lowered resting breathing rate more than meditation did, and the effect grew the more days people practiced. It works in part because a long exhale slows the heart through the vagus nerve, which is why one sigh calms you faster than a deep breath in.
how: Inhale through the nose, then take a second short sip of air on top to fill the lungs fully.
Let it all out slowly through the mouth, so the exhale lasts about twice as long as the inhale.
Repeat for five minutes, ideally at the same time each day; before a hard conversation or after the commute works well.
tip.src: Balban et al. · Cell Reports Medicine, 2023

markets.headline: Stocks slipped on Thursday as Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia and Treasury yields jumped on their first day back: the S&P 500 fell 0.35% to 7,592.40, Tesla rose 1.7% on SpaceX merger reports, Intel lost 2.1% and SpaceX closed flat ahead of Friday's Starship flight.
points: The S&P 500 fell 26.98 points (0.35%) to 7,592.40, the Nasdaq dropped 0.39% to 25,366.09 and the Dow lost 0.36% to 52,297.09, while the Russell 2000 bucked the trend with a 1.6% gain. The index erased a sharp opening drop and finished with modest losses; AP puts the S&P 500 up about 10.9% for 2026.

Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and director effective immediately, with CFO Colette Kress named interim CEO and Harvey Jones the board's first chair. NVDA opened down sharply, halved its loss and closed down 4.34% at 166.19; Truist and Craig-Hallum downgraded to Hold and Baird to Neutral, with Wedbush's Dan Ives valuing the stock at $225 without Huang versus $300 with him. Earnings are still due November 17. Rivals rallied: AMD jumped 5.9% to 585.30 after Bank of America lifted its target to $700 and William Blair upgraded to Outperform, and Broadcom also gained, while Intel, Marvell, Lumentum and Coherent fell.

Treasuries reopened after Veterans Day and sold off on Tuesday's hot CPI: the 10-year yield rose more than 13 bp to 5.125% and the 2-year jumped 15 bp to 4.879%, with oil prices also higher. CME FedWatch now prices a 100% chance of a December hike, roughly 87% for a quarter point and 13% for a half point. October PPI is due Friday, with economists expecting +0.4% month over month after September's 1.3%.

Tesla rose 6.61 (1.7%) to 397.45, its fifth straight gain, after Bloomberg reported that SpaceX-Tesla merger talks are progressing toward a possible December announcement. Intel fell 1.30 (2.1%) to 61.20 on about 80.6 million shares as Bank of America cut its target to $80 from $100 (Neutral) and the Huang news hit chip names. SpaceX swung from 137.85 to 147.60 intraday, popping on the Huang news (Musk reportedly eyeing the former Nvidia CEO) and a $74 billion AI-campus commitment, before closing up 0.19 (0.1%) at 139.94 ahead of Friday's Starship Flight 15 double-catch attempt; Polymarket puts the booster catch at 77% and the ship catch at 47%.

pick.name: Cerebras Systems
pick.theme: Wafer-scale AI chipmaker that just beat, raised its 2026 outlook and added Microsoft as a third hyperscaler customer
pick.what: Cerebras designs the Wafer Scale Engine, a dinner-plate-sized AI processor that keeps an entire model on one chip instead of spreading it across many GPUs, and sells it as CS-3 systems and through its own inference cloud. The company went public on Nasdaq in 2026 and competes with Nvidia and AMD for AI training and especially fast inference workloads.
pick.why: After the November 12 close Cerebras reported record Q3 GAAP revenue of $210.8 million (core revenue $230.9 million, up 70% year over year, versus roughly $215 million expected), raised full-year 2026 core revenue guidance to $940-960 million from $880-890 million, guided Q4 to $310-330 million and said it expects to triple revenue in 2027. It also announced a Microsoft Cloud agreement that Rosenblatt says brings its hyperscaler customer count to three and eases worries about dependence on OpenAI; the shares, which closed down 3.3% at 97.75 before the print, jumped 13-19% after hours and premarket. TipRanks shows a Strong Buy consensus with nine unanimous Buy ratings and an average target of $267.13, while MarketBeat's tally is Moderate Buy with a $261.80 consensus target; the stock sits about 75% below its 52-week high of 386.34 after a brutal fall slide. An idea to research, not a recommendation.
pick.risk: The stock has already lost roughly three quarters of its value from the high and hit an all-time low of 77.84 on November 5, so the volatility cuts both ways: options were pricing a 13.7% earnings move, and sources disagree on the size of the after-hours pop. Analysts have been slashing targets even while keeping Buy ratings (Morgan Stanley to $178 from $279, Needham to $200 from $300, UBS to $155), customer concentration around OpenAI remains high, it competes head-on with Nvidia and AMD, and a December Fed hike with the 10-year above 5% is a headwind for an unprofitable, high-multiple AI name.

btc.summary: Cowen's newest video, posted Thursday, is titled Bitcoin Q4 Dump Came Just the Same, and it is a victory lap after weeks of being told he was wrong: the fourth-quarter slide he has called for all year, the one that showed up in the midterm years 2014, 2018 and 2022, arrived on schedule once bitcoin fell back below the 50-week average and the stock market rolled over. His framing, repeated in a post the same day, is that the market always finds a way to convince people that this time is different, and that accepting back below the old range puts the fourth quarter back on its historical track. He still reads the move as driven by the correction in stocks rather than anything crypto-specific, and keeps his base case of a low later this quarter rather than a straight-line crash.

brief.lede: Jensen Huang resigned from Nvidia and Colette Kress is interim CEO, SoftBank led a $500 million round for Agile Robots, Bloomberg says a SpaceX-Tesla merger could be announced in December, and bitcoin broke below $70,000 overnight.

articles.title: SoftBank leads a $500 million round for Agile Robots at $8.5 billion
body: Munich-based Agile Robots said on Thursday it has raised **$500 million in a Series F round led by SoftBank**, valuing the company at **$8.5 billion**. Nvidia, Hitachi and T.Capital also invested, and the company said the round takes its total funding to about $2 billion. Reuters and Bloomberg carried the news on November 12 and the company confirmed it.

The round came in smaller than expected. Bloomberg had earlier reported that SoftBank was in talks to anchor a round of roughly $800 million, putting in more than $300 million itself. Even so, the valuation makes Agile the most valuable private robotics company in Europe, ahead of Neura Robotics and London-based Humanoid.

Agile says the money will go toward expansion in the United States, more engineers and additional production capacity, including in Germany. It opened a factory near Munich earlier this year that it says can build up to 10,000 legged and wheeled humanoids a year; reports put this year's expected output at **around 2,000 units**, with output possibly doubling or tripling in 2027.  Alongside the raise, Agile and Nvidia introduced the Agile ONE SN research platform, which pairs Agile's humanoid hardware with Nvidia's Isaac GR00T software.

The company has not disclosed revenue, so what underpins the $8.5 billion figure is unclear. Its robots are already in a lab trial at Audi's Ingolstadt plant, and Agile was one of the launch partners named by Google DeepMind for Gemini Robotics 2.5 earlier this week, which gives it a foothold on both the Nvidia and Google robot-AI stacks.

The deal lands days after a setback for SoftBank's wider robotics push. Chinese regulators blocked SoftBank's roughly $5.4 billion purchase of ABB's robotics division in early November, reportedly over concerns that robotics data would leave the country to train AI models. ABB says the two sides are still working on the sale, but China was the division's largest market.

For the industry, the signal is that late-stage humanoid money is still flowing at large valuations even as the ABB block shows how quickly geopolitics can reshape who owns what. The next things to watch are where Agile puts its US capacity and whether it publishes any production or deployment numbers to justify the price.

articles.title: ASUS builds its own humanoid to pack motherboard parts
body: ASUS has unveiled Gallop, its first humanoid robot, and is testing it on a packing station at one of its own contract-manufacturing factories, the company said in a blog post on November 13. The two-armed robot is learning to pack **15 small motherboard accessories**, many sealed in thin clear plastic bags, at a workstation built for human hands. ASUS's target is **99.5 percent task success within 20 seconds**, which it says is the same standard it holds a person to.

Gallop runs on a single Nvidia Jetson AGX Thor module and learns mostly by watching skilled workers, then practicing on the same parts. ASUS says the robot is aimed at repetitive, physically demanding stations that are hardest to staff rather than at replacing workers. Next steps include fitting its own dexterous hand, putting Gallop on wheels and showing it at Computex 2027; customer pilots are planned for 2027 and market availability for the second half of 2028. The 99.5 percent figure is a target, not a demonstrated result, and no price was given.

Chinese state media went a different direction. Xinhua and UBTech unveiled two life-size bionic humanoid news anchors, Xinyan and Xinyu, at the World Media Summit in Beijing on November 5, with a press release following on November 11. Filmmaker Zhang Yimou led the visual design; UBTech supplied the bionic skin, hardware, operating system and an emotional language model, while scripts come from Xinhua's AI current-affairs system. Xinhua calls them a world first.

Trade policy is the backdrop for every imported humanoid headed to a US factory. A J.P. Morgan report on November 12 flagged that President Trump's October 28 proclamation accepted a Section 232 finding that imported robotics and industrial machinery threaten national security. The proclamation set no tariffs; instead it opened a **180-day negotiation period**, with tariffs, quotas or investment incentives held in reserve depending on the outcome.

What it means: electronics makers with their own factories and Nvidia relationships are becoming humanoid vendors in their own right, and a mid-2027 update on the Section 232 talks will decide whether robots built in Taiwan, Germany or China face new costs at the US border.

articles.title: Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO; Kress takes over on an interim basis
body: Jensen Huang is out at Nvidia. The company said Thursday, November 12 that Huang **resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately**, and that chief financial officer Colette Kress will run the company as interim CEO while keeping the CFO job. The board also named director Harvey C. Jones as Nvidia's first-ever chair, splitting a role Huang had held since he co-founded the company in 1993, and said it will search for a permanent CEO among internal and external candidates.

The filing with the SEC says the board accepted the resignation on November 11, the night it met to weigh removing him. CNBC, citing a person familiar with the matter, described the outcome as an ouster rather than a voluntary exit. Huang admitted an affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang on November 8 after reports that US intelligence suspected her of spying for China; the New York Times then reported a second relationship with an Nvidia vice president, and Yahoo Finance's live coverage on Thursday said a third allegation had surfaced.

The stock swung hard. Shares fell **as much as 14.35% right after the open**, then clawed back most of that to **close down 4.34%**, per CNBC. CNN put the day's lost market value at roughly $182 billion.

Analysts split between relief and worry: Wedbush's Dan Ives said Kress will likely hold the interim role for about a year, while others warned the stock now carries a leadership discount because Huang was part of the investment thesis. Prediction-market traders have made Ian Buck, who runs Nvidia's data-center business, an early favorite for the permanent job, according to Fortune and Axios.

The fallout reaches beyond Nvidia. Bloomberg reported that Nvidia's roughly $10 billion commitment to Anthropic's IPO, part of the $26 billion private placement running alongside the offering, is now under fresh scrutiny with its champion gone.

What comes next is fast. Nvidia reports fiscal third-quarter results on Tuesday, November 17, which will be Kress's first call as interim CEO, and the Wachtell Lipton probe into possible compromise of company or national-security information is still open. For the chip trade, the question is whether a steady-hands finance chief can keep the roadmap and the customer relationships intact while the search runs.

articles.title: SpaceX-Tesla merger talks advance as Starship 15 waits on the FAA
body: Bloomberg reported on Thursday that merger talks between SpaceX and Tesla are progressing and that a deal could be announced **as soon as December**, citing people familiar with the matter; the companies have also discussed the announcement slipping into early 2027. Reuters carried the report and put SpaceX's market value at about $1.90 trillion and Tesla's at about $1.55 trillion, which would make it the largest deal ever. No terms, exchange ratio or governance structure has been reported, and neither company has commented.

Tesla shares rose 1.69 percent to close at **$397.45** on November 12, touching $401.22 intraday, while the Nasdaq slipped 0.39 percent. It was the fifth straight gain, a run of about 15.6 percent that also took in the Finland driver-assist approval and the Cybertruck reprieve. Electrek expects SpaceX to be the acquirer rather than the other way around.

Musk said on SpaceX's third-quarter call that a merger would be a good idea and that both boards have formed special committees of independent directors. The obstacles Bloomberg's sources cite are Tesla's China operations, which would need to be ring-fenced, and SpaceX's US defense contracts. Tesla's annual meeting is on December 3, but the October proxy includes no merger vote, so any deal would need a separate shareholder meeting.

Separately, Starship Flight 15 is still set for today, with the window opening at **2:45 PM PT** and running 75 minutes. Booster 22 is due back at the Starbase pad about six and a half minutes after liftoff and Ship 42 would attempt the first-ever ship catch after deploying 26 Starlink V3 satellites; a double catch would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system. As of Thursday the FAA had still not published the license modification covering the ship's return over populated areas, and SpaceX lists the flight as pending regulatory approval.

Smaller Tesla items from November 12: the Full Self-Driving (Supervised) referral program expanded to Canada and Mexico, and Tesla opened a Semi service center in Laredo, Texas. The unscripted Optimus video Musk promised on the third-quarter call has not appeared.
What to watch: whether SpaceX launches on time or slips again on paperwork, and whether either board confirms the merger timetable before December 3.

articles.title: Bitcoin breaks $70,000 as liquidations and yields bite
body: Bitcoin broke below **$70,000 early Friday, November 13, for the first time since August 20**, extending a two-day slide. Bloomberg reported the coin fell as much as 5.4% to about $67,628 before steadying, and Quartz had it near $69,342, down about 3% on the day. Thursday had already seen it lose the $72,000 level.

The immediate trigger was forced selling. KuCoin counted roughly $622 million of crypto liquidations as the $70,000 level gave way, and 24-hour tallies ran to about $1.23 billion, with more than 96% of bitcoin liquidations hitting traders who had bet on higher prices. An analyst quoted by Decrypt called it a concentrated liquidation of leveraged longs but said the deeper issue is demand that has been weakening for weeks.

The macro backdrop did the rest. Bloomberg tied the drop to inflation worries and higher interest rates, and XTB noted the 10-year Treasury yield posted its sharpest one-day rise since April 2025 alongside a firmer dollar. Quartz linked the move to the tech-stock selloff around Nvidia's CEO exit, and stablecoin supply has slipped below $280 billion, meaning less cash sitting on exchanges. The crypto fear and greed index is back in extreme fear.

Spot ETFs are still leaking, though more slowly. Preliminary Farside data for November 12 showed a **sixth straight day of net outflows at about $47.7 million**, with BlackRock's IBIT and Fidelity's FBTC not yet reported, so the final figure could change; Bitwise's BITB led the day at $26.4 million out.

Strategy felt the MSCI decision in its share price. **MSTR fell 6.49% Thursday to $114.41**, Cointelegraph reported, a day after MSCI confirmed it will drop the company from its global indexes at the November 30 close. The company repeated that the rule is "discriminatory, arbitrary and misguided" and asked MSCI to withdraw it, while arguing that MSCI-linked funds hold only about 13 million shares, or 3.1% of shares outstanding, so forced selling should be modest.

What to watch: the October producer price report lands at 5:30 AM PT Friday. A hot print would firm up December hike odds and test whether the overnight low near $67,000 holds, while a soft one gives the market its first excuse in a week to bounce.

articles.title: OpenAI ships security agents as Anthropic's IPO week nears
body: OpenAI used its Cyber at the Frontier livestream on Thursday, November 12 to turn last week's GPT-6 Cyber model into products. **Daybreak Red Team**, now taking early-access requests, sends a team of agents to probe a customer's web application with access to its source code, validates what it finds and retests patches. **Daybreak Defense Factory**, in research preview as a plugin in Codex and ChatGPT, scans a connected GitHub repository, traces each vulnerability through the code, tries to reproduce it in an isolated environment, and drafts a patch with a test for an engineer to review before a pull request is opened.

Defense Factory can also take in findings from scanners such as Wiz, Snyk and Endor Labs, so it slots into existing security pipelines rather than replacing them, SecurityWeek reported. OpenAI gave no pricing. The Register, cited by other outlets, said the underlying model is GPT-6 Cyber, which OpenAI released November 5 to selected customers after rating it Critical for cybersecurity risk under its preparedness framework, meaning it is held behind vetting rather than offered openly.

Across town, Anthropic's IPO moved into its final week with a new wrinkle. Bloomberg reported Thursday that Nvidia's roughly $10 billion share of the **$26 billion private placement** alongside the offering is under scrutiny now that Jensen Huang, who pushed the deal, is gone. Demand is not the problem: Investing.com reported orders at about six times the shares on offer. The offering of 825 million shares at $70 to $78 is expected to price Wednesday, November 18 and trade on Nasdaq as ANT the next day.

On the research side, Google DeepMind released AlphaGenome 2 on November 11. The model reads a megabase of DNA plus a target cell state and predicts how a variant changes gene activity in that specific cell type rather than averaged across tissues; on a 28-cell-type immune dataset it recovered roughly twice as many causal variants as its predecessor, per Interesting Engineering.

For the coming week the calendar is tight: Nvidia's results on November 17 will set the mood a day before Anthropic prices, and OpenAI's cyber push gives security teams a concrete thing to test rather than a roadmap.

articles.title: The brain's sleep rinse fades with age; five drugs share a metabolite
body: The brain's overnight rinse cycle weakens with age, and now there are human numbers behind it. A Nature Aging paper from the Lewis lab at MIT, published Thursday, November 13, measured the slow waves of cerebrospinal fluid that wash through the brain during sleep and found them **significantly reduced in older adults compared with younger ones**. Earlier studies disagreed, partly because they did not record flow during actual sleep.

The decline was a group trend, not a rule: some older participants kept normal fluid waves, so the loss is not inevitable. The same lab reported earlier that short bursts of pink noise during sleep boosted the waves in younger adults, an approach not yet tried in older people. The waves are thought to help clear waste such as amyloid, the protein that accumulates in Alzheimer's disease.

A second paper asked what proven lifespan treatments have in common. In Frontiers in Aging, Badenoch and colleagues profiled metabolites across tissues of genetically diverse male mice given rapamycin, acarbose, 17-alpha-estradiol, canagliflozin or 40% calorie restriction. One molecule stood out: **ergothioneine, a dietary antioxidant from mushrooms, rose with all five treatments in plasma and brain** and with four of five in muscle. The link is an association; the authors suggest feeding more ergothioneine as the next test.

Two other items dated November 12. Utah biomedical engineers reported in Aging Cell that a protein called ZNF865 is depleted in aging and damaged spinal discs and may protect the spine, a candidate CRISPR target for age-related back pain, with any treatment far off. And Fight Aging highlighted a Neurology study from Karolinska that tracked 352 cognitively healthy 70-year-old women with MRI for five years: longer lifetime estrogen exposure and past hormone therapy went with healthier small vessels and white matter. It is observational, with self-reported exposure.

The thread this week is mechanism rather than lifespan headlines: fluid clearance measurable in a clinic, a metabolite sold as a supplement, and a checkpoint pathway with approved drugs in hand. None is a treatment yet, but all three can reach human tests sooner than most mouse-lifespan results.

vocab.def: Glowing or flickering softly over a surface; of wit or light, playing lightly and brilliantly without heat.

cards.b: Latin lambere ('to lick'): a flame that licks across a surface without burning it
glowing, flickering, luminous, softly radiant
late sun on the bay, a gas flame on a stove, a friend's light and quick humor

examples: By 4:30 the lambent light off the salt ponds made even the parking lot look painted.
Her lambent wit kept the review going for two hours without anyone noticing the time.
vocab.ex: By 4:30 the lambent light off the salt ponds made even the parking lot look painted.

vocab.def: Casually unconcerned; carefree in a way that shows a light, almost careless lack of worry.

cards.b: French insouciant, from in- ('not') and soucier ('to care'), from Latin sollicitare ('to disturb')
nonchalant, carefree, breezy, unbothered
a surfer shrugging at a wipeout, a founder joking through a bad quarter, a cat on a warm car hood

examples: He gave an insouciant shrug when the demo robot fell over, and the room relaxed with him.
There's an insouciant charm to a city that closes its best street for a Sunday market.
vocab.ex: He gave an insouciant shrug when the demo robot fell over, and the room relaxed with him.

vocab.def: The tendency to see meaningful patterns or connections in random or unrelated data.

cards.b: Coined by German psychiatrist Klaus Conrad in 1958, from Greek apo- ('away from') and phainein ('to show')
patternicity, false pattern, seeing faces in clouds
a backtest that only looks predictive, a 'trend' in three data points, a conspiracy theory

examples: Three green days in a row isn't a signal; that's apophenia talking.
Robot logs invite apophenia: every glitch looks like a pattern until you count.
vocab.ex: Three green days in a row isn't a signal; that's apophenia talking.

vocab.def: Calm self-confidence, especially in a tense or difficult situation.

cards.b: French 'à plomb', 'according to the plumb line', meaning upright and steady
poise, composure, assurance
handling pressure gracefully: a demo gone wrong, a hard question, a surprise

examples: She fielded the hostile question with perfect aplomb.
The robot demo failed, but he recovered with aplomb.
vocab.ex: She fielded the hostile question with perfect aplomb.

vocab.def: Impossible to avoid or escape; certain to happen no matter what you do.

cards.b: Latin 'ineluctabilis', from in- (not) + eluctari (to struggle out of)
inescapable, unavoidable, inevitable
fate, deadlines, or facts that no amount of effort changes

examples: The ineluctable arrival of winter sent everyone indoors.
He felt the ineluctable pull of the old neighborhood.
vocab.ex: The ineluctable arrival of winter sent everyone indoors.

vocab.def: A very fine, light, delicate material, like spider silk; or anything that feels that thin and airy.

cards.b: Middle English; often traced to 'goose summer', the warm autumn days when floating spider silk is seen
filmy, sheer, diaphanous
cobwebs in morning light, thin fabric, or something fragile and barely there

examples: Gossamer threads of spider silk caught the low autumn sun.
She wore a gossamer scarf that moved with every breath of wind.
vocab.ex: Gossamer threads of spider silk caught the low autumn sun.

vocab.def: Relating to twilight; describing animals that are most active at dawn and dusk.

cards.b: From Latin crepusculum, 'twilight'
dusky, dim, twilit
animals like rabbits, deer and owls that move around at dawn and dusk, or any soft low light

examples: The crepuscular glow made the whole street look gold.
Rabbits are crepuscular, so the best time to spot them is just after sunrise.
vocab.ex: The crepuscular glow made the whole street look gold.

spanish.note: Cañón is literally 'cannon' or 'canyon', but in Mexico 'está cañón' means something is hard, heavy or impressive: a tough exam, a brutal commute, a wild story. Tone decides whether it's a complaint or admiration.

cards.en: Same idea, cruder; only with close friends

parts.en: a cannon shot; a hit song

dialog.en: How did the interview go?

dialog.es: Está cañón, me hicieron tres pruebas técnicas.
dialog.en: It's intense, they gave me three technical tests.
And did you pass?

dialog.es: Creo que sí, pero me dejaron hecho polvo.
dialog.en: I think so, but they wore me out.

spanish.use: Say it when someone describes a hard day, a steep trail or a big bill, or with a grin when a demo blows you away.

spanish.note: Literally 'what a bear', but in Mexico it's the everyday way to say 'how embarrassing' or 'how awkward', about yourself or someone else. 'Hacer el oso' is to embarrass yourself in public.

cards.en: I'm embarrassed / it makes me shy

parts.en: to make a fool of yourself

dialog.es: Le dije 'mamá' a la maestra enfrente de todos.
dialog.en: I called the teacher 'mom' in front of everyone.
How embarrassing! And what did you do?

dialog.es: Nada, me puse rojo y me senté.
dialog.en: Nothing, I turned red and sat down.

dialog.es: Ya ni modo, mañana nadie se acuerda.
dialog.en: Oh well, tomorrow nobody will remember.

spanish.use: Say it with a wince when someone trips, waves at the wrong person or replies-all by mistake.

spanish.note: Literally 'to little', but in Mexico it's the everyday way to say 'really?' or 'you're kidding' when something surprises you. Flip it to '¿a poco no?' and it means 'right?' or 'isn't it?'

cards.en: No way! / Don't make it up!

dialog.en: They offered me a job in Guadalajara.
Really? That's great!
Yes, I start in January.
Well, congratulations, we have to celebrate.

spanish.use: Say it with raised eyebrows the moment someone surprises you.

spanish.note: Literally 'it's of hairs', but in Mexican slang 'de pelos' means excellent or really good. Use it for food, plans, music, anything you like.

dialog.en: Did you try the new tacos?
Yes, they're awesome!
Shall we go again tomorrow?
Deal, we'll go tomorrow.

spanish.use: Say it when something is better than you expected.

spanish.meaning: I can't be bothered to go out
spanish.note: 'Flojera' is laziness, but in Mexican Spanish 'me da flojera' is a relaxed way to say you don't feel like doing something. It isn't a harsh judgment of yourself. Swap in any verb: 'me da flojera cocinar'.

dialog.en: Shall we go to the movies tonight?
Ugh, I can't be bothered to go out.

dialog.es: Pedimos pizza y vemos algo en casa.
dialog.en: We'll order pizza and watch something at home.
Now that's a great idea!

spanish.use: Say it when a plan sounds fine but your couch sounds better.

options: I can't be bothered to go out

spanish.meaning: I like your friend (he's easy to get along with)
spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish 'caer bien' means that someone strikes you as likeable. It's about the person's vibe, not romance. The opposite is 'caer mal' or, more bluntly, 'caer gordo'.

dialog.en: What did you think of Luis?

dialog.es: Me cae bien tu amigo, es muy relajado.
dialog.en: I like your friend, he's very laid back.
Yeah, he always makes me laugh.

dialog.es: Invítalo otra vez, me cae bien.
dialog.en: Invite him again, I like him.

spanish.use: Say it after meeting someone you got along with, to tell a friend your first impression.

spanish.note: In Mexican Spanish, 'ya estuvo' closes something off. It can mean 'that's done', 'we're all set', or, with the right tone, 'that's enough'. Context and your voice do the work.

dialog.en: Do you still need anything from the store?
No, that's everything, thanks.
Sure? There's still time.
Yes, we're done. Let's go.

spanish.use: Say it when a task is finished, an order is complete, or you want to politely end something.

phrases: Ni modo, ya será para la próxima
Ahorita vengo, voy por unos tacos

dare.title: Take Caltrain one stop too far
dare.why: The first real storm of the season blows through around midday and should be done by 3, so tonight is a clean, washed evening. Walk to the Mountain View station after work, ride north, and get off at a stop you have never actually left, say Burlingame or San Carlos, and walk the main street for half an hour before picking the restaurant with the longest line. One rule: no maps app once you step off the train.

place.name: Mountain View Caltrain station
place.sub: Downtown Mountain View, trains about every 20 to 30 minutes

dare.worth: You have passed those towns a hundred times and they are still a blank. One wander turns a name on a departures board into a place you know, and the ride home after rain smells like a different Peninsula.

swap.title: Watch a rocket try to land twice
swap.why: If the FAA signs off, Starship's launch window opens at 2:45 PM today and the booster should be back at the tower about seven minutes after liftoff, with the first-ever attempt to catch the ship near the end of the flight. Put the SpaceX stream on a big screen, say out loud what you think will happen before each catch, and do nothing else while it plays.
swap.worth: Nobody has ever recovered a whole orbital rocket at the pad. If it works today you will remember where you watched it, and if it blows up you will still have seen the attempt live.
